Updated 24 August 2026 · FABRIOZA Editorial Team

So read it for the numbers rather than the ranking: where each option is based, what it will actually make for you, and the minimum you have to commit to.

Every figure below is what that company publicly states about itself as of August 2026. Minimums and lead times change, so confirm directly before you order.

1. FABRIOZA — Per-Sport Programmes, 15–20 Set Minimums

Based: Sialkot, Pakistan
Minimum order: 15–20 sets (team sports) · 20-piece trials
Lead time: 2–3 weeks + 3–7 days DDP

Yes, this is us — judge it against the rest of the list. We run sixteen dedicated sport programmes (basketball, baseball, soccer, wrestling, volleyball, lacrosse and more) rather than one generic activewear line, which means the patterns, fabric weights and minimums are set per sport. ISO 9001 certified and amfori BSCI audited.

Best for: A single squad that needs 15–20 sets, or a brand wanting to test a design at 20 pieces before committing.

The catch: We are a factory, not a US dealer — if you need uniforms in your hands in seven days, a domestic supplier will beat us.

2. Ready One — Certified Sialkot Factory, MOQ 50

Based: Sialkot, Pakistan
Minimum order: 50 units per style per colourway
Lead time: Not publicly stated

States on its site that it was founded in 2012, holds ISO 9001, BSCI and SEDEX certification, produces 100,000–150,000 units per month and ships DDP to 40+ countries. One of the most visible Pakistani manufacturers in English-language search, with a broad activewear and blanks range.

Best for: Brands wanting a heavily certified Pakistani factory with serious monthly capacity behind them.

The catch: The 50-per-style-per-colourway minimum is higher than team sports usually need — a single side rarely orders 50 of one colourway.

3. Wooter Apparel — US-Based Custom Team Uniforms

Based: Staten Island, New York, USA
Minimum order: Not publicly stated for bulk; sub-10 jersey orders via a separate shop
Lead time: 3–4 weeks, or 2–3 weeks rush

A well-known US custom team uniform supplier covering basketball, football, soccer, baseball and more, with an online builder and a rush option. Domestic shipping removes customs entirely.

Best for: US teams that want a familiar domestic supplier and are willing to pay for the convenience and speed.

The catch: US-based production carries US pricing. For a club buying every season, the per-unit gap against a direct factory is significant.

4. Nike Team, Adidas Team and Under Armour Team

Based: USA, via authorised dealers
Minimum order: Set by the dealer, typically 12–24 sets
Lead time: Varies by dealer and programme

The brand-name route. You order through an authorised team dealer rather than the brand, choosing from that season's uniform programme with your colours, numbers and names applied.

Best for: Schools and programmes where the badge on the jersey matters as much as the jersey, and budget allows for it.

The catch: You are buying a template, not a custom garment — design freedom is limited to what the programme offers, at the highest price point on this list.

5. Champro, Boombah and ProLook — US Team Catalogue Brands

Based: USA
Minimum order: Varies by brand and product line
Lead time: Typically 3–6 weeks

The middle tier of the American team market: established catalogue brands with both stock and custom sublimated lines, sold direct and through dealers. Reliable, well-understood by US coaches and athletic directors.

Best for: US school and club programmes that want a known brand, a catalogue to pick from, and someone local to call.

The catch: Custom options are usually chosen from set templates, and unit pricing sits well above factory-direct.

6. Chinese OEM Sportswear Factories

Based: Mainly Guangdong and Fujian, China
Minimum order: Commonly 100–500 pieces per style
Lead time: 3–5 weeks + shipping

The largest sportswear manufacturing base in the world, reachable directly or through sourcing platforms. Enormous capability and the lowest unit prices at volume.

Best for: Brands ordering several hundred units per style, where unit price dominates the decision.

The catch: Minimums are usually far above a single team's needs, and landed cost after freight, duty and agent fees often erases the headline saving — check the DDP number, not the FOB one.

7. Sourcing Platforms (Alibaba, Made-in-China, Foursource)

Based: Global marketplaces
Minimum order: Set by each listed supplier
Lead time: Varies by supplier

Marketplaces rather than manufacturers. Useful for discovering factories and comparing quotes quickly, with escrow-style payment protection on some platforms.

Best for: Early-stage sourcing when you do not yet know which factories exist for your product.

The catch: You are talking to whoever paid for visibility, and many listings are trading companies rather than factories. Verify who actually owns the machines before you place an order.

8. Local Print Shops + Blank Garments

Based: Your own city
Minimum order: Often as low as 1–12 pieces
Lead time: Days to 2 weeks

Buy blank jerseys wholesale and have a local shop print or embroider them. No manufacturing relationship required.

Best for: A one-off tournament team, a charity match, or testing a design before committing to production.

The catch: You are limited to whatever blanks exist — no custom cut, no sublimated all-over design, no private labelling, and per-unit cost stays flat no matter how many you order.

9. Regional Specialists (Portugal, Turkey, Mexico)

Based: Europe and North America
Minimum order: Typically 100–300 per style
Lead time: 3–5 weeks

Nearshore options for brands prioritising shorter shipping and EU or USMCA trade terms over the lowest unit price.

Best for: European or North American brands where lead time and proximity outweigh cost per unit.

The catch: Minimums are higher than Pakistani factories and pricing sits between Asia and domestic production.

How to Choose

If you are one team needing one set of kit — a direct factory with 15–20 set minimums or a local print shop are your only realistic options. Most of this list will not take an order that small.

If you are a brand testing a design — find a factory with a genuine trial tier. Ordering 20 pieces to check quality is far cheaper than discovering a fit problem across 300 units.

If you need it next week — buy domestic. No overseas factory, including us, beats a local supplier on pure speed.

If you are ordering several hundred per style — get quotes from both Pakistan and China, and insist on a landed DDP figure from each. The FOB comparison is the one that misleads people.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the lowest minimum order for custom sportswear?

Direct factories in Pakistan currently offer the lowest workable minimums for team sport: 15-20 sets per design, which suits a single squad. Local print shops go lower still - as few as one piece - but only on blank garments, with no custom cut or all-over sublimation. Chinese factories typically start at 100-500 per style.

Is it cheaper to manufacture sportswear in Pakistan or China?

On FOB unit price the two are close, and China is often lower at high volume. On landed cost the picture changes: freight, import duty, brokerage and agent fees are frequently added to a Chinese quote, while many Pakistani factories quote DDP with duties included. Compare the delivered price, not the factory price.

How long does custom sportswear take to manufacture?

Roughly 4-6 weeks end to end from most direct factories: 24-48 hours for a design mockup, 5-7 business days for a physical sample, 2-3 weeks production, and 3-7 days express delivery. US domestic suppliers typically quote 3-4 weeks with rush options at 2-3.

What certifications should a sportswear manufacturer have?

ISO 9001 for quality management and a social compliance audit such as amfori BSCI or SEDEX are the meaningful baseline. Ask for the certificate number and the issuing body rather than accepting a logo on a website - certificates are verifiable, logos are not.

Should I use a sourcing platform or contact a factory directly?

Platforms are useful for discovery when you do not know which factories exist. Once you have a shortlist, dealing directly removes a margin layer and gets you to the people who actually control production. Confirm whoever you speak to owns the machines rather than subcontracting the order.
